review_notes: Martin safety +1/medium: I tested this as overstated, because his public-defense stint was only three years before mixed civil/criminal practice [S3]. It still holds. His career was defense-side throughout its criminal component [S5], and he self-reports presiding over the Shoreline/Kenmore Community Court, which connects defendants to housing and treatment 'while reducing repeat offenses' [S1]. The court's page and his Shoreline assignment partly corroborate that role [S7]. He takes no bail position, so medium, not high. Below Trasen's high is consistent. Martin experience -1/medium: a sitting judge by unanimous merit-selection appointment [S2], but only about nine months on the bench, so medium rather than Masaniai's (SW4) -1/high is the right distinction. Rose-Akins safety -1/medium: six years as a misdemeanor prosecutor and seven advising SPD [S2], mirroring Tse and Walls. Her prosecutorial work with Mental Health and Community Court participants is noted in the basis and does not reach a diversion position, and her pro tem release-setting reports describe no approach. Rose-Akins experience 0/medium: I tested it against Tse's -1, since both are ex-prosecutor pro tems running on readiness. Rose-Akins has less pro tem tenure (2+ years, self-reported) [S2] and is challenging a sitting judge, which matches Steinmetz's (SW4) 0/medium. Upheld. No judicial score for either is correct: 'steady judgment' and 'listen first, decide last' are boilerplate [S1]. The Stranger and King County Democrats endorsements are correctly unused in any basis. Summary/highlight flags: (1) Rose-Akins highlight 3, 'her claimed KCBA rating is not on KCBA's page', implies a contradiction. KCBA's 2026 page does not list this race for either candidate [S4], and Martin's KCBA rating also comes only from the council appointment file. Suggested wording: 'her claimed KCBA rating could not be checked (KCBA's 2026 page omits this race)'. (2) The race_blurb names only Martin's endorsers (King County Democrats, The Stranger) and gives Rose-Akins only a fundraising figure. For balance, add her pamphlet-listed endorsers, for example three Supreme Court justices and the Attorney General [S1], or drop the endorsement clause.
